scenario.title: 稱讚別人、接受稱讚
scenario.context: 台灣人被稱讚時的直覺是否認：「沒有啦」「哪有」。但在英文裡，否認稱讚等於說對方眼光不好。這個單元學怎麼大方地說 thank you，也學怎麼用 so / such 讓稱讚更有力。

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.en: Minz, your presentation was so good. The client loved it.
lines.zh: Minz，你的簡報超棒，客戶很喜歡。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Thank you! I was so nervous, but I'm glad it went well.
lines.zh: 謝謝！我超緊張的，但很高興進行得很順利。

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.en: Seriously, you nailed it. The mood board was on point.
lines.zh: 說真的你表現完美，情緒板做得超到位。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Thanks, Daniel. That means a lot coming from you.
lines.zh: 謝謝 Daniel，你這樣說對我意義重大。

lines.speaker: Karen
lines.en: It was such a clear story. Where did you learn to present like that?
lines.zh: 故事好清楚。你在哪學會這樣報告的？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I've been practicing a lot. And Amy gave me some really helpful feedback.
lines.zh: 我一直在練習。而且 Amy 給了我很有幫助的回饋。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: Whoa, look at you! You're looking sharp today.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Thanks! I have a job interview this afternoon.

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: That suit fits you so well. Where'd you get it?
lines.zh: 那套西裝好合身，在哪買的？

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Thanks, I actually got it tailored. It was such a good deal.
lines.zh: 謝謝，其實是訂做的，價錢超划算。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: You're killing it lately. New haircut, new suit, interviews…
lines.zh: 你最近好猛，新髮型、新西裝、面試……

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.en: Ha, I appreciate it. Wish me luck!

patterns.en: Thank you, that's so kind of you.
Thanks! I worked really hard on it.
patterns.note: 大方承認努力，不用謙虛否認

patterns.en: I couldn't have done it without the team.
I love your ___. Where did you get it?
patterns.zh: 我好喜歡你的 ___，在哪買的？

patterns.en: You did a great job on ___.
That color looks great on you.
You have such a good eye.

chinglish.wrong: No, no, no, I'm not good at all.
chinglish.right: Thank you! I'm glad you liked it.
chinglish.why: 中文用否認表達謙虛，英文直接否認稱讚會讓對方尷尬，好像他判斷錯了。說 thank you 就是最好的謙虛。

chinglish.wrong: Your English is so good! — No, my English is very poor.
chinglish.right: Thanks! I'm still working on it.
chinglish.why: 想謙虛可以加一句「我還在努力」，但不要否定對方。

chinglish.right: It's such a good idea. / The idea is so good.
chinglish.why: 名詞前面用 such (a)，單獨形容詞前用 so。
文法沒錯，但對同事說 handsome 可能有點私人。稱讚打扮用 looking sharp / great 比較安全。

grammar.title: 回應稱讚＋so / such
grammar.oneLiner: so + 形容詞 / 副詞；such (a) + (形容詞) + 名詞。回應稱讚時先說 thank you。
whenToUse: so + 形容詞：It was so good. / You're so talented.
so + 副詞：You presented so clearly.
such a + 形容詞 + 單數名詞：It was such a clear story.
such + 形容詞 + 複數 / 不可數名詞：They're such nice people. / It was such good advice.
so / such… that…（結果）：It was so good that I watched it twice.
回應稱讚的公式：Thank you + (感受 / 分享功勞 / 補充細節)。
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 中文的「好」「超」「這麼」放在形容詞或名詞前都一樣：「好棒」「好棒的點子」。英文要看後面是不是名詞，選 so 或 such。台灣人常說 so good idea 或 such good，其實只要記住：看到名詞就用 such。

examples.correct: It was such a great presentation.
They gave me such helpful feedback.
examples.incorrect: They gave me such a helpful feedback.

examples.correct: The food was so good that we ordered more.
A: Great job! B: Thanks, I really appreciate that.
examples.incorrect: A: Great job! B: No, it's nothing.

options: Thanks! I'm glad it went well.

slang.usage: You're killing it! = 你表現太好了。也說 You killed it!

risk.note: 正面稱讚，同事間也常用。

examples.en: Your Instagram is killing it lately!
examples.zh: 你的 IG 最近超紅！

examples.en: You killed it on stage last night.

slang.usage: 形容穿搭、妝容、作品、時機剛剛好。Your outfit is on point.

risk.note: 口語，工作上對熟同事用沒問題。

examples.en: Your eyeliner is on point today.
examples.zh: 你今天眼線畫得超完美。

examples.en: The timing of that joke was on point.
examples.zh: 那個笑話的時機抓得超準。

slang.usage: You nailed it! / I nailed the interview. 也常被反諷用：做很爛時自嘲 Nailed it.

risk.note: 正面時很安全，注意語調以免被當反諷。

examples.en: You nailed the interview! They want to hire you.
examples.zh: 你面試超完美！他們要錄取你。

examples.en: (Looking at a burnt cake) Nailed it.

slang.usage: 稱讚別人打扮得體、有精神，男女都可用。

risk.note: 比 handsome / beautiful 中性，職場稱讚打扮很安全。

examples.zh: 好帥！今天有重要會議嗎？

examples.en: You're looking sharp in that blazer.
examples.zh: 你穿那件西裝外套很有型。
